en.title: Netflix Drops New 'What's Hot' Hub for Buzzy Titles and Top 10s
en.summary: Netflix has unveiled a new 'What's Hot' hub, a dedicated destination for trending content, including Top 10 lists and genre favorites. This move signals a significant shift in how the streamer organizes and surfaces its most popular titles for a global audience.
en.body:
Netflix is making it easier than ever to find out what everyone else is watching. The streaming giant has launched a new 'What's Hot' hub, a centralized destination designed to showcase its buzziest titles, most popular Top 10 lists, and genre favorites. Accessible via a dedicated URL and integrated across TV and mobile devices, this new feature aims to cut through the noise and guide viewers directly to content that's currently dominating conversations and watchlists. The hub prominently features an orange "HOT" wordmark and is populated with rows of curated content, a clear evolution from the more static genre pages of the past.

This initiative appears to be part of a broader strategy by Netflix to refine its user interface and content discovery algorithms. The 'What's Hot' hub is built primarily around popularity data, pulling from existing Top 10 rows, regional hits, and genre-specific charts. While not featuring hand-picked thematic collections, some rows, like "Buzzing Now," are designed to capture content experiencing a surge in popularity, whether it's a brand-new release or an older favorite making a comeback. On a recent check in the US, "Buzzing Now" included a mix of titles like **Lupin** (new episodes), **Gossip Girl** (recently added), and **Yellowjackets**, alongside older shows like **Heroes** and **Victoria**, the latter carrying a "Leaving Soon" tag. The hub also showcases the current Top 10 Films and Series in specific regions, alongside "Hits From Around the World," offering a global snapshot of viewer engagement.

## A New Compass for Content Discovery

The introduction of the 'What's Hot' hub is more than just a cosmetic update; it’s a strategic play to leverage FOMO and social proof. For dedicated binge-watchers and series fans, this means a more direct line to the shows and movies that are igniting online discussions and driving cultural moments. The inclusion of labels such as "New Season," "New Episode," "Recently Added," and "Leaving Soon" adds a layer of urgency and context, informing viewers about the lifecycle of the content they're considering. This move aligns with Netflix's ongoing experiments with its TV interface, which have focused on "modules" and special rows that highlight trending or timely content. By consolidating these elements into a single, easily accessible hub, Netflix is essentially providing a dynamic, real-time guide to what's resonating with its massive subscriber base.

## What Fans Are Saying

While direct fan commentary on this specific hub is still emerging, the concept taps into a long-standing desire for curated recommendations that reflect current zeitgeist. The frustration of scrolling endlessly through options is a common refrain among streaming audiences. This hub offers a solution by surfacing titles that are demonstrably popular and generating buzz. For fans invested in the longevity and success of their favorite shows, seeing them highlighted in "Buzzing Now" or on Top 10 lists can be a reassuring indicator of their continued relevance and potential for future seasons. Conversely, the "Leaving Soon" tags serve as a crucial heads-up, prompting fans to catch up before a beloved title departs the platform.

## What's Next

As Netflix continues to refine its content discovery tools, the 'What's Hot' hub is likely to evolve. While currently focused on popularity metrics, future iterations might incorporate more personalized elements or deeper dives into regional trends. Fans should keep an eye on how these modules are updated and how they influence viewing habits across the platform.

content_raw: Netflix has a new hub page for what’s trending right now. It’s the latest dedicated destination to launch on the service, just a week after the KPop Demon Hunters fan hub, and it arrives as Netflix reworks how its rows and playlists are put together. A new page now sits at netflix.com/browse/genre/83112341 and will feature on your TV and mobile devices. It has a large orange “HOT” wordmark across the top and a stack of rows below, all built around one idea: what people are watching on Netflix right now expanding on the top 10 rows which have been present on Netflix since 2020 (although it began testing back in 2019).  You won’t find hand-picked themes or mood-based collections here. Most of the rows come from popularity data, like the Top 10s, regional hits and genre charts. The few rows that aren’t straight charts, such as “Buzzing Now,” are still clearly about momentum. What’s inside the What’s Hot hub? The hub has a bunch of different rows but here’s how it looked on November 12th in the US (which is the only region currently re told): Buzzing Now: A mix of new releases and older shows getting a fresh push, including The Hunting Wives (new season, coming soon), Lupin (new episodes), Gossip Girl (recently added), Yellowjackets , Heroes , Best of the Best , and Victoria , which carries a “Leaving Soon” tag. Top 10 Films in the US Today: Led by Reminders of Him , The Gospel of Christmas , Funny Money: The Dane Cook Story , Carolina Caroline , A Dog’s Perfect Christmas , The Croods , and The Day After Tomorrow . Top 10 Series in the US Today: Taken: Natalee Holloway , Black Doves , From , The Body , Nobody Wants This , Power , and The Neighborhood . Hits From Around the World: Anaesthesia , Below , Godzilla Minus One , 100 Days of Deception , One Year to Live, Buy a Man , Doctor X: Mafia in White , and Where the Mask Ends . Several of the K-dramas show “New Episode” labels for their weekly drops. Popular in Horror: Stranger Things , Interview with the Vampire , Midnight Mass , Haunted Hotel , Hannibal , Frankenstein , and Teen Wolf , which is leaving Netflix after only a year . Popular in Romance: Bridgerton , A Discovery of Witches , Sweet Magnolias , Voicemails for Isabelle , Sullivan’s Crossing , My Life with the Walter Boys , and Ransom Canyon . Popular in Documentaries & Reality: Mostly presidential docuseries ( Theodore Roosevelt , FDR , Washington , Abraham Lincoln , and Grant ), plus Bob Ross: Happy Accidents, Betrayal & Greed and Miracle: The Boys of ‘80 . Popular in Anime: One Piece (new season, coming soon), Fullmetal Alchemist: Brotherhood , Detective Conan , The Apothecary Diaries , The Ramparts of Ice , Steel Ball Run: JoJo’s Bizarre Adventure , and Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2 . Top 10 Kids Shows: Doozie’s Doghouse , Danny Go! , Ms. Rachel , Gabby’s Dollhouse , Salish & Jordan Matter , and more. Top 10 Kids Movies: Rounds out the page.
